title: Pages printed their own markup: double-escaped entities in reader copy
detail: Guide fields that the renderer escapes (title, standfirst, intro, verdict) had been authored with HTML entity markup, so the escaping pass double-encoded them and readers saw the markup itself: thermometer-accuracy.html showed a visible plusmn entity where the sentence means plus-or-minus half a degree, and the first-week and Thanksgiving guides each showed a stray mdash entity. The page source looked correct, so this was found by reading the built pages rather than the registers. Fixed in the generator: escaped reader fields decode named and numeric entities to characters before escaping, every page rebuilt clean, and the gate now unescapes each page's visible text and fails on any entity sequence left. The same rule caught the leak in three further renderers during integration with another session's pass.
owner_status: Corrected; the gate rule covers all pages, not only the ones that were visibly wrong.

title: P-04 accuracy claim and in-box certificate are still seller statements, not verified facts

None of that has been confirmed against a manufacturer document or a test, and the USDA FSIS factsheet notes only that most thermometers are accurate within 2 to 4 degrees F, which is a baseline for the category rather than a judgement on this unit. The site publishes the figure as the seller's claim, attributed and dated, and the ice-water test guide explains how to check it on your own unit. No page calls it verified.
owner_status: Open; needs the manufacturer specification sheet or the certificate itself to move.

title: Unresolved git merge-conflict markers were committed to main inside the stylesheet
detail: On 2026-11-20 session 19dbf5e2 found three conflict markers left in the file on main: '<<<<<<< HEAD' at line 684, '=======' at 753 and '>>>>>>> origin/main' at 834 of assets/style.css. Both sides' rule blocks were intact between the markers, so the markers were deleted and both sides kept (session 35973829 removed the same markers independently the same day; this branch carried its own copy of the repair through the merge, so the two fixes agree), which leaves the stylesheet parseable and the brace count balanced (479/479). A browser skips a stray marker line, so the damage was invisible rather than catastrophic - but CSS error recovery can swallow the rule after an unmatched token, which is how the November layer lost .hero earlier. Request to the owner of scripts/check_site.py (T-30, session 57fc3be0): fail the build when any tracked file contains a merge marker. This session did not edit that file, per its claim. Follow-up the same day: a stray '=======' separator survived in the merged file, which is why the request became a rule instead of staying a note.
owner_status: Repaired on 2026-11-20, and the requested gate rule now exists: scripts/check_site.py fails any tracked source file containing a conflict-marker line. A second instance (a stray '=======' line left in the same file by a later merge) was found by that rule's first run, removed, and recorded here so the class stays closed.

title: Five products shared two images, and the images are renderings, not photographs
detail: Until this pass, all five product cards and all five product pages pointed at two image files, so the same photo of three fryers appeared under a thermometer card's neighbour and under every air fryer. That is the clearest remaining tell of a generated site, and a shop cannot lean on it. Five distinct renderings were commissioned for this site (assets/photos/p01..p05) and wired per product, plus a real og:image per product page. Two things follow, and both need an owner: first, a rendering is an editorial approximation, not an accurate picture of the SKU, so every one is captioned as illustrative and no Amazon photography is used (the site has no licence for it, and PA-API or Creators API imagery requires the owner's approved credentials); second, if the owner prefers no synthetic imagery at all on product pages, the fix is to remove the figures rather than to source photographs, which is a decision, not an automation.
owner_status: Published and labelled. Owner decision requested: keep labelled renderings, go to illustration-only SVG, or wait for API-supplied imagery (SG-13, SG-15).

title: The test suite hardcoded the page count, so publishing anything broke CI

The assertion now derives the expected number from the HTML files on disk, and a second test checks that every guide record produces a page, appears in sitemap.xml, feed.xml and findability.txt, ends on a tagged product line, and carries no escaped-entity artefacts.

detail: The seasonal guides printed a hand-written '7 min read' claim beside the generator's computed 'about 2 min of reading': two numbers for one thing, the unmeasured one first. The generator's own estimate also ignored the tables, checklists and source panels that make up a third of a guide, so it under-counted every page it printed — a 970-word guide was labelled 2 minutes. Fixed in the merge: the asserted numbers are gone, and the surviving measure (build_site.guide_words, contributed by session 93894704) counts the kicker, title, sub, intro, verdict, every section and the extra block. This session's duplicate helper was deleted rather than kept alongside it, so one formula produces the single figure the gate now requires on each guide.
owner_status: Repaired on 2026-11-20. One measured figure per guide, and a test asserts it is the only one on the page.

title: A guide quotes OSHA, but osha.gov is not on the source-host allowlist
detail: The certification guide quotes OSHA's own description of the Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory programme and links https://www.osha.gov/nationally-recognized-testing-laboratory-program, fetched and read on 2026-11-20. It was deliberately not added to data/sources.json: the build gate's I-4 rule documents that admitting a host to the official-source allowlist is an owner decision rather than a fix, so this session linked the document on the page instead of widening the gate for itself. Owner action: add 'www.osha.gov' to OFFICIAL_SOURCE_HOSTS in scripts/check_site.py (one line) if the federal source is acceptable, then register the row as S27.
owner_status: Queued for owner decision (Q-29). Nothing on the site depends on the register entry; the guide's link is live and its wording is attributed to OSHA.

title: Half the build gate ran after the report, so those rules had never failed a build
detail: scripts/check_site.py printed its verdict and called sys.exit(1) in the middle of the file. Everything written below that line — the reader-voice rules (no register codes, no chunk citations, no internal headings on buyer pages), the verification-table 'every row links to a source' rule, the findability.txt coverage rule and the provenance-field checks — executed after the verdict had already been printed and never affected the exit code. They had been passing for days because nothing read their result, not because the site satisfied them. Moved on 2026-11-20 so the report is the last thing the script does. The first honest run produced 97 real problems: 44 verification rows with no source link (the page claimed 'The official listing link is in every table row', which was untrue for three of its tables), 10 audit artefacts on the five product pages, and a coverage rule that compared paths wrongly. All 97 are fixed in the same pass (FLG-065, FLG-066), and the site now passes the whole file.
owner_status: Repaired on 2026-11-20. Request to whoever owns the gate next: the report block should be structurally last — a function that prints the verdict and exits, called from the end of the file — so no future rule can be appended into dead code.

title: Two gate rules could never fail, so the problems they described stayed unfixed
detail: Found while repairing FLG-064. (1) The findability.txt coverage rule tested f'{BASE}{page}' where `page` is an absolute filesystem path, producing strings like 'https://site/Affil2//home/user/repo/index.html' that no file can contain; the rule passed only because its result was never read. Fixed to compare the repo-relative path, and findability.txt does list all 43 submitted pages. (2) The verification rule that requires a source link in every register row was equally unread: three of the page's tables (the live pass per-product reads, the new-observations table, the corrections table) had no link column at all, while the page's own prose promised a link in every row. The tables now carry Source / Read against / Record columns, and the claim is true.
owner_status: Repaired on 2026-11-20, in the generator rather than by loosening the rules.

title: Every product page printed the same provenance record twice, once in audit language
detail: The product template rendered both intent_table() and ledger_block(): the same five fields, once as an internal register extract — headed 'Product-intent confirmation record', carrying bare codes such as '(FLG-001)', '(FLG-004)' and 'see FLG-022' — and once in the shop-voice version the reader-voice pass had introduced. The buyer saw the audit copy first. This is the exact pattern the owner asked to have removed, and it survived because the rule that forbids it was unreachable (FLG-064). The audit table is no longer emitted on buyer pages; intent_table() is kept for internal surfaces and now has a test asserting it still agrees with the register, so it cannot quietly drift out of use. The five required fields — submitted link, intended ASIN, observed redirect target, Special Link we publish, confirmation date, plus the Associates test status — remain on every product page, in reader language, exactly once.
owner_status: Repaired on 2026-11-20 with a regression test. Nothing was deleted from the record: the codes live on flagged.html, the facts live on the product page.

title: The site prints no prices, so it must not imply a price comparison either
detail: A guide verdict written on 2026-11-20 recommended 'the cheaper appliance in this category'. Nothing on the site states a price, and the site refuses to: Amazon's Program Policies permit price and availability display only when Amazon serves the link or the data comes through the API. A word like 'cheaper' asserts the same fact in a vaguer coat, and the build gate had no rule about it, because every rule so far was written against a dollar sign. Reworded to 'the simpler one-zone basket on this page', which is a statement about the appliance the register can support. scripts/check_site.py now fails any reader surface containing cheaper, more expensive, cost-effective, best value, value for money, worth the money, priced low/below/under, inexpensive or affordable; verified by planting a sentence on index.html and watching the gate reject it.
owner_status: Repaired and gated on 2026-11-20. If the owner later approves PA-API or Creators API access (SG-13, SG-31), this rule is the one to retire first — with real data, not adjectives.

title: The register's product keys were printed inside shopper sentences
detail: P-01 to P-05 are keys in data/products.json. They appeared as visible text on reader pages: the front page and shop tables opened with the key as a row label, every compare column repeated it under the brand, and two product pages said 'If you want to leave the room, you want P-05 instead' and 'If the app or network is a problem for you, P-04 is the safer buy'. The reader-voice rules only looked for FLG-xxx codes and crawl citations, so this passed three audits. Fixed in the generator: a `named()` helper substitutes each key with the words the listing itself uses (the Chefman dual-basket, the Emeril French-door oven, the Chefman 8-quart, the ThermoMaven, the CHEF iQ Sense), the overview table's first column became Brand instead of ID, and the compare header dropped the prefix. No value changed. scripts/check_site.py now fails any reader page whose visible text contains a product key, verified by planting 'Compare P-03 first.' on a product page and watching the build reject it. Audit surfaces (verification.html, flagged.html, sources.html, campaign-ledger.html) keep the keys on purpose, because there they are the point.
owner_status: Repaired and gated on 2026-11-20. Nothing in the register was edited.
